deployment_target_confirmed: L2/Arbitrum reseed. Verified: contracts/beanstalk/init/reseed/L2/ exists (ReseedBean/Barn/Field/Silo/Sun/Whitelist/InternalBalances) and contracts/beanstalk/init/reseed/L1/ReseedL2Migration.sol drives the L1->L2 migration. ReseedInternalBalances + ReseedL2Migration reference arbitrum/L2. C.sol and LibWeth hardcode Ethereum-mainnet addresses that are consumed by oracle/wrap/pipeline/well logic running on the L2 target.
create2_analysis: ReseedBean deploys BEAN/UNRIPE_BEAN/UNRIPE_LP via `new BeanstalkERC20{salt}(address(this), name, symbol)` and the three Wells via `new ERC1967Proxy{salt}(impl, init)`. CREATE2 address = keccak256(0xff ++ deployer ++ salt ++ keccak256(initcode)). Here deployer = the ReseedBean contract on Arbitrum (NOT the original mainnet deployer/CreateX used to mine the 0xBEA0.../0x1BEA... vanity addresses), AND the initcode hash embeds constructor arg address(this) = ReseedBean's L2 address. Both the deployer and the initcode differ from whatever produced the mainnet vanity addresses, so the reseed-deployed instances will NOT land on the hardcoded mainnet constants. Therefore C.BEAN / C.UNRIPE_BEAN / C.UNRIPE_LP / C.BEAN_ETH_WELL / C.BEAN_WSTETH_WELL are NOT reproduced cross-chain by this reseed logic -> the CREATE2-determinism FALSE_POSITIVE hypothesis FAILS. Additionally CP2_U_BEAN_ETH_WELL_IMPLMENTATION / CP2_U_BEAN_WSTETH_WELL_IMPLMENTATION = address(0) (TODO placeholders), so the well proxies cannot even deploy correctly. These are real-bug leads, not deterministic-correct constants.
